### Owner goal clarification for T01

On 2026-09-06 the owner added a fifth core goal to the accepted design:
give the agent more space to exercise judgment. Preserve the accepted
[whiteboard](../solution-whiteboard.md) as historical evidence; this linked
clarification supplies the additional goal for T01 source reconciliation.

| Core goal | Intended outcome |
| --- | --- |
| Clear boundaries | Make protected constraints and authority explicit |
| Stable outcomes | Demonstrate the agreed result regardless of execution approach |
| Key information only | Retain information needed for decisions, verification and recovery |
| Proportional effort | Match process and evidence to value, complexity and risk |
| Agent discretion | Let the agent choose methods, sequencing and safe recovery within approved boundaries, without unnecessary procedural prescriptions or repeated permission requests |

Agent discretion is an explicit goal, not merely an implementation technique.
It does not expand permissions or weaken outcome, safety, evidence or required
human-acceptance boundaries. The existing error-handling framework below is
one application. Source implementation and conformance verification remain
pending; this records the owner's direction, not a new completed review.

### Error-handling clarification for T01

On 2026-09-06 the owner clarified FC02/FC03: handling an agent's own mistake
belongs within existing error handling, not a new rule or separate framework.
Integrate this into the existing
[recovery and exception triage](../../../docs/batch-review-and-recovery.md#recovery-without-restarting-everything)
guidance and reconcile its consumers as part of T01.

Diagnosis should lead to correction, verification and continuation when the
agent can restore approved intent safely within existing authority. An agent
mistake alone is not a reason to request human approval again. Critical
mismatches, conflicting authority or changes requiring a new owner decision
still stop affected work. Existing quality, evidence, review and merge controls
remain; this clarification does not claim the implementation is complete.

The owner further clarified that triage belongs to this same error-handling
framework. Distinguish an agent mistake from a genuine project or playbook gap
using the governing intent and observed evidence, not merely a failed check.

| Triage outcome | Handling and tracking |
| --- | --- |
| Agent mistake | Correct and verify within authority; no issue solely for the mistake |
| Genuine project gap | Link or open a deduplicated issue in the project's tracker for evaluation and follow-up |
| Genuine playbook gap | Link or open a deduplicated issue in the verified playbook upstream for evaluation and follow-up |
| Uncertain cause | Preserve uncertainty and perform safe bounded diagnosis; do not label an unconfirmed gap as proven |

Cause and operational severity are separate: an issue does not automatically
stop safe work, and an agent-caused safety failure still requires a stop.
Isolate affected work where possible; stop the whole workflow only when the
impact cannot be safely contained. Continue unaffected work within authority.
Issue tracking does not substitute for recovery verification or authorize bypass.
Use existing reporting permissions and privacy protections; if filing is blocked,
retain a pending report in the existing recovery record rather than claiming it
was filed. Reconcile existing project/playbook exception-routing guidance in T01,
without introducing a separate reporting framework or duplicate progress record.

Use the T01 mapping omission as a recovery example: distinguish repairing the
record of an approved task from changing its dependencies or requiring its
future output. Verify both safe continuation and justified escalation in the
existing recovery acceptance cases, without introducing another gate or ledger.
